At trailing P/E of 28× (at the lower bound of the 28–45× industrials sector range) and EV/EBITDA of 20.7× (below the broad-market peer median of 23.3× at P44), the stock screens as FAIR to modestly cheap — forward P/E at 21.5× below trailing confirms earnings growth is being priced in, and the EV/EBITDA yardstick (most appropriate for capital-goods names per the sector card) also supports a fair verdict. The biggest risk is that the growth recovery is a single-quarter data point after prolonged weakness, agriculture equipment remains soft (-6.4% YoY), there is no management guidance to anchor the trajectory, and industrials stocks historically de-rate 30–50% on any government capex-pause signal — a real risk given the current RISK_OFF macro regime with FII sustained selling.

PNB Housing Finance is a mid-sized housing lender with loan AUM of Rs 94,124 cr and strong reported asset quality (GNPA down from 0.95% in Q1 to 0.91%, NNPA 0.55%, capital adequacy 27.03%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 11.5% to Rs 4,687 cr, but PAT rose only 5.3% to Rs 1,174 cr, slowing sharply from +18.3% in FY26; subtracting Q1 from H1 implies Q2 revenue growth of about +13.7% and PAT growth of about +5.7%, so margins are being squeezed (26.9% in FY26 to 25.0% in H1), while the flagged slide from a 94.4% margin and +27.6% revenue growth comes from a faulty 9M FY26 row and should be ignored. On P/B plus ROE, the right yardstick for a lender, 1.36x book is fair and leans cheap, because ROE of 11.6% (H1 annualised, filings) to 12.7% (TTM) straddles the 12% cheap line; trailing P/E of 11.43x is inside the 18-28x NBFC range's lower bound only as context, the broad-market peer rank is not a like-for-like comparison, and the 9.68x forward P/E needs roughly 15% earnings growth against about 5% now. The biggest risk is that those growth expectations are cut if margins stay under pressure, and H1 NIM and management guidance were not available to test this, with the 81% reliance on market funding adding to the risk.

fundamental.thesis: Elgi Equipments is a Coimbatore-based compressed-air equipment manufacturer (92% compressor revenue) with a growing global footprint — 51% of Q1FY27 revenue came from international markets (North America ₹261cr, Europe ₹151cr) — positioning it as a rare mid-cap Indian industrial with genuine export scale. fundamental.thesis: Great Eastern Shipping earns most of its money from owning and chartering tankers and dry-bulk carriers, with a smaller offshore segment, so the sector card's order-book framework fits poorly and earnings depend on charter rates. Q1FY27 revenue rose 66.9% YoY to Rs 2,005 cr and PAT rose 159.3% to Rs 1,309 cr, with revenue growth swinging from -20.3% a year earlier and quarterly PAT derived from the cumulative figures climbing from Rs 504 cr to Rs 582 cr, Rs 812 cr, about Rs 1,045 cr and Rs 1,309 cr; about Rs 125 cr of the latest PAT came from ship-sale gains, and the 57.2% PAT margin is on total income (about 65% on reported revenue). Using EV/EBITDA and P/B with ROE as the yardstick for a capital-intensive cyclical, the stock looks cheap at 4.7x EV/EBITDA and 1.19x book with 18.8% ROE, alongside a 6.9x trailing P/E, though the broad-market peer ranks (P2-P6) say little because there are no tight shipping peers, and the snapshot's 330% dividend yield and 6.41 debt/equity look like unit errors given about Rs 799 cr of debt and Rs 3,009 cr of net cash. The main risk is that low multiples on near-peak earnings can be a cyclical value trap, as the forward P/E above trailing implies lower earnings ahead, and Q2FY27 results due on 6 November could quickly change this view since the latest filed numbers are over three months old.

fundamental.thesis: Kalpataru Projects is a mid-cap engineering and construction contractor working across power transmission and other infrastructure and energy projects, with 250+ projects in 75 countries and a record order book of ₹71,846 cr, about 2.6x trailing revenue. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, the stock looks cheap at 11.15x (P15, against a broad-market median of 23.3x) and 22.46x trailing P/E (below the 28-45x Industrials range), but the broad-market peer set is a weak comparison for a low-margin contractor and the price is already at 90.8% of its 52-week range, so I hold this view with moderate confidence. fundamental.thesis: Atul Ltd is a diversified specialty chemicals conglomerate — 42+ subsidiaries spanning agrochemicals, polymers, aromatic intermediates, and life sciences — that serves both domestic and export markets, with meaningful China+1 optionality in specialty chemical supply chains. Q1FY27 saw a sharp inflection: consolidated revenue accelerated to +25.0% YoY (₹1,848 cr vs ₹1,478 cr in Q1FY26, up from a steady ~12% pace through FY26), while PAT surged 91.8% YoY to ₹254 cr with EBITDA margin expanding to 23.2% from ~17.8% — the Performance & Other Chemicals segment led at +33.8% YoY, though Life Science Chemicals remained sluggish at only +4.5% YoY, a concentration risk worth watching. At trailing P/E of 28.2× (above the 12–22× Materials sector median but at P38 in the broad market, below the 35.2× broad-market median) and EV/EBITDA of 17.36× (P32 vs a 23.3× broad-market median), the stock grades as fairly valued — forward P/E of 21.47× is a meaningful discount to trailing, confirming consensus expects earnings to continue growing, and the 30/90-day EPS revision of +6.6% is supportive. The primary risk is elevated Debt/Equity of 2.91× in a rising crude ($90.41/bbl) and weakening INR (96.05/USD) environment, which could pressure chemical input costs and unwind the margin recovery if the Performance segment's volume momentum decelerates.

fundamental.thesis: Gland Pharma is a mid-cap injectables maker: it develops and manufactures injectable drugs for partners (B2B) and makes them to order for other drug companies (CDMO). It sells mainly into the US, where Q1 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to ₹981 cr, and owns the European CDMO Cenexi. In Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue was ₹1,800 cr, up 20% YoY, and PAT was ₹317 cr, up 47% YoY, for a PAT margin of 17.6%. Revenue growth has picked up from +6–7% a year ago to +20–23% over the last three quarters, and PAT margin has widened from 12–14% to about 18%, though revenue grew only 3% and PAT fell 14% versus Q4. Using the pharma P/E yardstick, a trailing P/E of 35.3x is inside the 28–40x sector range and at the median of its broad-market peers (P50). EV/EBITDA of 20.1x and P/B of 3.5x are below the peer median, and the forward P/E of 24.1x prices in continued growth, so overall valuation is fair, not cheap. The stock also sits at 76% of its 52-week range. Management raised its medium-term growth target to about 20% CAGR from 15% and estimates are up 5–7% over 90 days, but the biggest risks are that the strong US growth slows (the US is reviewing whether generic drugs should also face tariffs) and an overhang from a promoter-side Fosun shareholding disclosure that arrived alongside a board change, ahead of Q2 results on 6 Nov.

LT Foods is a mid-cap food company tagged FMCG, and its results show fast sales growth on thin margins (about 11% EBITDA and under 6% PAT). The newest usable quarter is Q1 FY27, because Q2/H1 FY27 was filed on 2026-10-27 but its numbers were not extracted: revenue was Rs 3,161 cr (+26.0% YoY), with growth steady at about 24-26% since 9M FY26, split between 12% volume and 11% price/mix, while PAT of Rs 183 cr rose only +9.0%, after +2.2% for FY26, and gross margin slipped from 34.4% to 32.6%. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick, with P/E as a cross-check, the stock looks cheap at 10.4x EV/EBITDA (P11, 55% below the median) and 21.5x trailing P/E (P24, below the 40-60x FMCG range), although the comparison set is the broad market rather than close peers, and 13.3x forward P/E implies about 60% EPS growth that recent profit growth does not support. The biggest risk is that the low multiple correctly reflects sales growth that is not reaching profit, especially as FY EPS estimates were cut 5.5% over the last 30 days and the Q2 results remain unread here; the pre-computed deceleration signal, Q2 FY26 row (Rs 277 cr revenue, 59.1% margin), 105% dividend yield and 7.5x P/B (inconsistent with 21.5x P/E and 14.9% ROE, which imply about 3.2x) all look like data errors and were ignored.

fundamental.thesis: Castrol India is the market-leading branded lubricants company, with a 167,000-outlet distribution network that grew its rural reach to 46,000 outlets, so it behaves more like a consumer-brands business than the oil PSUs in the Energy sector card. For 9M CY26, revenue rose 20.3% YoY to ₹5,151 cr but PAT grew only 8.7% to ₹766 cr; backing out H1 (₹3,417 cr revenue, ₹590 cr PAT) implies the Sep-quarter revenue grew about 27% to roughly ₹1,734 cr while PAT fell about 22% to roughly ₹176 cr, so PAT margin dropped from 18.6% in the Jun quarter to about 10%, and the implied EBITDA margin of about 15% sits well below management's 21-24% target band. Using EV/EBITDA and P/E as the yardstick (not the PSU 'policy-priced' P/E-plus-yield framework), the stock trades at 17.7x trailing P/E and 11.9x EV/EBITDA, about 50% below the broad-market median (P18/P17), but trailing earnings include the stronger H1 and FY-EPS estimates were cut 4.9% over 30 days, so I grade it fair rather than cheap until margins stabilise. H1FY27 revenue surged +67.6% YoY to ₹77,199 cr and PAT exploded +697.6% YoY to ₹2,846 cr (PAT margin 3.7%), a dramatic recovery from the near-zero-profit FY26 base (PAT margin 1.8%), with EBITDA margin expanding to 6.6% on strong throughput and higher product realisations — though a fire incident at the CHT unit on 30-Sep-2026 provisionally cost ₹118 cr and creates near-term operational uncertainty. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive refinery (per sector card guidance for PSU OMCs/refiners), MRPL trades at 5.97× EV/EBITDA versus a broad-market median of 23.3× — placing it at P3 in its peer universe — making it structurally cheap, though the sector card explicitly cautions this discount is 'policy-priced' (permanent policy risk, not a valuation error); trailing P/E of 14.5× sits at the upper end of the PSU OMC range (6–10× + yield), but the forward P/E collapses to 3.4×, implying the street is pricing in a very strong FY27 full-year earnings recovery. The key risk is that elevated crude at $97.97/bbl directly compresses refining marketing margins for OMC-adjacent refiners, estimate revisions are sharply negative (-9.6% 30d, -21.2% next-FY 90d) signalling analyst concern about GRM sustainability, and the CHT fire adds operational/insurance settlement uncertainty over the next 1–2 quarters.

ACME Solar is a mid-sized renewable power producer with about 2,990 MW operating at Q1 FY27 and about 5,080 MW under construction, mostly on long-term contracts with central government-backed buyers, plus a growing battery storage business. H1 FY27 revenue rose 78.2% YoY to Rs 1,745 cr and PAT rose 105% to Rs 504 cr; subtracting Q1 implies Q2 revenue of about Rs 791 cr (about +100% YoY, but about -17% QoQ) and PAT of about Rs 269 cr, so the pre-computed 'accelerating' and 'expanding' signals are unreliable because they mix half-year, quarterly and annual periods, and the 97.7% H1 EBITDA margin implies an impossible Q2 margin above 100% of revenue unless other income or a definition mismatch is inflating it. fundamental.thesis: Anand Rathi Wealth is a capital-light HNI/UHNWI wealth management distributor earning trail commissions and distribution fees on a growing AUM base — an asset-light model that structurally warrants premium P/E multiples over traditional lenders. H1FY27 revenue grew +17.4% YoY to ₹646 cr (decelerating from FY26's +22.3%), while PAT surged +26.4% YoY to ₹322 cr with PAT margin expanding sharply to 49.8% from 34.5% in FY26, suggesting strong operating leverage — though this margin step-up from ~34% to ~50% in a single half-year warrants scrutiny for one-off items and seasonal AUM tailwinds. The stock trades at a trailing P/E of 80.3× and P/B of 36.78× — at P88 and P100 respectively vs the broad 499-stock market — with sell-side mean targets implying −26.8% downside and zero buy recommendations from only 2 analysts, while the 52-week position at 95.1% of range signals the stock is priced for near-perfection; using EV/EBITDA of 56.3× as the primary yardstick (per sector card for capital-light/platform-adjacent names), this is unambiguously expensive versus any reasonable comparable. The single largest risk is valuation derating from extreme multiples if AUM growth decelerates or equity markets correct, compounded by recent promoter pledge disclosures (SAST Reg 31 filings on Oct 16) which are a governance flag for a MIDCAP, thin sell-side coverage, below-1.0 CFO/PAT ratio (0.71×), and a high reported D/E of 8.25 whose nature warrants clarification.

fundamental.thesis: Cholamandalam Financial Holdings is the Murugappa Group's holding company; most of its value comes from its stake in Cholamandalam Investment & Finance (CIFCL, a vehicle and SME lender) plus Chola MS General Insurance, and 54.9% of group profit belongs to minority shareholders of those subsidiaries rather than to this company. In Q1FY27, consolidated revenue rose 19.5% YoY to ₹11,114 cr and profit attributable to shareholders rose 39.3% to ₹806 cr (a 7.2% margin), driven by CIFCL (AUM up 23% to ₹2.54L cr, PAT up 46%). Revenue growth has slowed gently from +21.8% to +19.5% over the trend window, and AUM growth has eased from 23% to 21–23%, while the insurance arm is lagging (premium up only 6%, PAT up 7.6%). The 'expanding' PAT-margin signal in the trend table is unreliable because annual and 9M rows appear to include minority shareholders' profit while quarterly rows do not. On the holding-company yardstick (P/B against ROE, with the card's normal 40–60% holding-company discount), a P/B of 1.86x with an implied ROE in the high teens, a trailing P/E of 10.8x against the 18–28x NBFC range, and a forward P/E of 8.0x put the stock at the cheap end even after allowing for that structural discount, and it sits at the 30% mark of its 52-week range. The biggest risks are that most of the value flows through CIFCL's credit cycle and the insurer's motor loss ratio, and that Q2FY27 results are due on 2026-11-06, in a risk-off market where foreign investors are concentrating their selling on Financials.

fundamental.thesis: HDB Financial Services is a large-scale NBFC and HDFC Bank subsidiary providing retail, commercial vehicle, and enterprise loans across a ₹1.31 lakh crore asset base, with strong parentage constituting its primary competitive moat and funding advantage. Revenue growth has decelerated from a peak of +21.4% (Q3FY26) to +10.3% in H1 FY27 with loan growth similarly slowing from 14.1% to ~11%, while PAT recovered sharply to +36.2% YoY (₹1,565 cr in H1 FY27 vs -2% in H1 FY26) as GNPA improved from 2.81% to 2.43% and Net NPA from 1.34% to 1.09% — partially offset by structurally elevated credit costs (2.58% in FY26) and deeply negative cash conversion (CFO/PAT -0.34×), which flag earnings quality concerns. Using the P/B+ROE lender yardstick mandated by the sector card, P/B 2.79× against ROE 13.9% places the stock in fair territory (not cheap: P/B > 1.5×; not expensive: P/B < 3× with ROE > 12%); peer-relative ranking at P27 in the broad market and a ~40% discount to sector median P/B, combined with forward P/E 14.7× vs trailing 22.5×, suggest the market has already priced in a meaningful earnings recovery. The primary risk is that loan/AUM growth deceleration (tracking toward low-double-digits) persists in a RISK_OFF macro environment with rising crude costs and an elevated credit cost base, stalling the earnings normalisation that currently drives the bull case.

Aurobindo Pharma is a large, export-led generics maker with about 44% of revenue from the US, 31% from Europe and only 8% from India. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.9% YoY to Rs 10,263 cr and PAT rose 32.5% to Rs 1,124 cr, accelerating from +8.4% and +7.6% in Q3 FY26, but Q2 includes the first full quarter of Lannett (consolidated from June 29, 2026), so organic growth is lower, and the reported Q2 EBITDA margin slipped from 23.0% to 21.0% QoQ (the quarterly margins do not reconcile with the 22.8% H1 figure, so this needs checking). On P/E and EV/EBITDA, the stock looks cheap at 24.0x trailing P/E (below the 28-40x sector range and the 36.4x peer median, P15) and 12.0x EV/EBITDA (peer median 21.4x, P0), but some discount is deserved given its US generics exposure and 9.9% ROE, and at about 85% of its 52-week range the easy re-rating may be behind it; H1 cash conversion is solid at 1.52x CFO/PAT, while the snapshot's 27% dividend yield and 21.31 debt/equity look like data errors and were ignored (the company reports a net cash position of USD 189M). The biggest risk is US margin and revenue durability: US revenue fell 13% in the latest reading available (Q4 FY26), no Q2 US growth figure or guidance was extracted, and the pending US review of generics tariffs remains unresolved.

fundamental.thesis: BSE is India's oldest stock exchange and a capital-markets infrastructure monopoly, earning revenues through transaction charges, listing fees, clearing/settlement, and investment income — it is not a traditional bank, so the relevant yardstick is P/E and EV/EBITDA (not P/B+ROE). Q1FY27 revenue grew +63.5% YoY to ₹1,566 cr and PAT grew +62.1% YoY to ₹873 cr at a 55.7% margin; while the absolute growth rate is still exceptional, the trajectory has decelerated from +116% in FY25, and PAT margins are broadly stable (55.7% vs 56.3% a year ago) rather than meaningfully expanding. At 48.1× trailing P/E (P68 vs broad peers) and EV/EBITDA of 28.4× (P63), the stock screens as fair against headline P/E metrics, but the forward P/E at 37.8× sits at P78 (expensive), P/B at 17.4× is at P94 (extremely elevated even for an asset-light exchange model), and sell-side EPS estimates have been cut sharply over the past 90 days (FY-EPS −6.6%, next-FY −9.8%) — a classic pre-derating signal that makes the 'fair' grade conditional on growth sustaining. The single biggest risk is that BSE's transaction-charge revenues are directly levered to equity market volumes and IPO activity, both of which face acute pressure from FII outflows of ₹44,000+ cr over 30 days, a RISK_OFF macro regime, and rising regulatory contribution costs (₹193 cr, +66% YoY), which could compress earnings faster than consensus currently models.

fundamental.thesis: Union Bank of India is a large public-sector lender, and its asset quality and loan growth are clearly getting better. In Q2 FY27, total income rose only +3.2% YoY to ₹32,809 cr, but PAT jumped +29.9% to ₹5,537 cr, pushing the PAT margin up to 16.9% from 13.4% a year ago. Under the hood the trend is clean: NIM rose from 2.67% to 2.86% over four quarters, gross NPA fell from 3.29% to 2.42%, net NPA fell to 0.42%, credit cost is low at 0.21%, and loan growth sped up from about 5% to about 13% YoY. Using the P/B-plus-ROE yardstick for lenders (P/E is ignored for banks), the stock trades at 1.01× book against a 15.7% TTM ROE (17.2% in Q2), so it is cheap. That reading is backed by a bottom-3rd-percentile rank on P/B. The main caution is that profits are rising much faster than income, which leans on low provisions and margin gains that may not last as rates reset, and 164 fraud cases (₹1,206 cr, nearly all already provided for) are a reminder of PSU governance and underwriting risk.

fundamental.thesis: 3M India is the listed Indian subsidiary of 3M Company (US), operating across four segments — Safety & Industrial, Transportation & Electronics, Healthcare, and Consumer — a diversified industrial-technology business leveraged to India's manufacturing expansion and domestic consumption themes. Revenue re-accelerated to +19.0% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹1,423 cr, 5th consecutive double-digit quarter), but earnings quality is poor: the reported PAT of ₹233 cr and 16.4% margin include a ₹73 cr exceptional land-sale gain, core EBITDA actually fell 2.7% YoY despite 19% topline growth, PBT before exceptionals declined 4.3% YoY, and the Transportation & Electronics segment margin collapsed 703 bps to 13.5% due to INR/USD headwinds — a clear deterioration of underlying operating profitability. At a trailing P/E of 64.1× and EV/EBITDA of 36.5× — both materially above the Industrials sector median (28–45× P/E) and placing the stock at P80 on P/E and P77 on EV/EBITDA vs. broader market peers — the valuation grades expensive, with earnings recovery already embedded in the 42.2× forward P/E; the high Debt/Equity of 9.6× and 86% YoY surge in finance costs compound the balance-sheet risk. The primary risk is that INR depreciation and segment-margin compression persist into Q2FY27, and with no management guidance provided, any disappointment against elevated consensus expectations could trigger a sharp de-rating from peak multiples.

IPCA Laboratories is a mid-sized drugmaker with a chronic-focused India branded business (about 45% of H1 FY27 revenue, ranked 16th domestically) plus exports of formulations and APIs, including its Unichem business. H1 FY27 revenue rose 17.1% to Rs 5,698 cr and PAT rose 50.7% to Rs 814 cr, with EBITDA margin up 280 bps to 22.9%, ahead of the 22-22.3% FY27 guidance; however, subtracting Q1 implies Q2 revenue of about Rs 2,910 cr, up about 13.8%, so growth slowed from +20.8% in Q1 despite the pre-computed 'accelerating' label, though it remains well above the +5.0% to +6.5% of Q3-Q4 FY26. Using P/E and EV/EBITDA as the yardsticks for a branded formulations business, valuation is fair: trailing P/E of 38.0x is near the top of the 28-40x sector range and at P69 of peers, EV/EBITDA of 22.6x is at P54, and with the stock at 96% of its 52-week range and only 2.2% below the mean analyst target, upside looks limited even with FY EPS estimates up 8.6% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that earnings quality is softening as CFO/PAT fell to 0.70x from 1.51x and FCF fell to Rs 130 cr from Rs 319 cr; the snapshot's 8.49 debt/equity and 31% dividend yield look like data errors given net debt/EBITDA of about 0.02x, so neither is used here.

Revenue recovered sharply to ₹1,484 cr in Q1 FY27 (+41.9% YoY, accelerating from the -24.9% trough of 9M FY2025), but this top-line bounce has not translated into operating profits: the fertilizer segment PBIT margin sits at -1.86%, the Q1 FY27 operating loss before finance costs was ₹36.51 cr, and the headline PAT of ₹3 cr (0.21% margin) is a statistical artefact of non-operating income rather than genuine operational recovery — full-year FY26 PAT was -₹40 cr. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per the sector card), FACT trades at 120.63× vs a fertilizer/chemicals cyclical mid-cycle norm of 5–8×, ranks P99 among 403 broad-market peers, and carries a P/B of 36.81× on a near-zero ROE — this is unambiguously expensive; the ₹50,886 cr market cap is disconnected from any demonstrated earnings power. The single largest risk is the compounding of a post-Q1 raw-material supply shock (West Asia geopolitical disruptions already causing plant shutdowns) on top of extreme financial leverage (D/E 295×) where quarterly finance costs of ₹61.98 cr structurally exceed operating income, leaving zero buffer for further stress.

Anupam Rasayan is a midcap specialty chemicals maker with 14 consolidated entities across India, the US, Europe, Japan and the Middle East, and its recent growth is partly acquisition-led, including Jayhawk and the consolidation of Tanfac. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 34.8% YoY to Rs 655 cr, down from +149% in Q2 FY26, while PAT rose only 5.7% to Rs 51 cr and PAT margin fell from 9.87% to 7.67% as finance costs rose 37.9% and depreciation 82.7%; I disregard the pre-computed 'accelerating' and 'expanding' labels because they mix annual and quarterly periods, and Q1 FY26, Q4 FY25 and the Q2 FY27 results due at the 6 Nov board meeting are missing from the table. Using EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for chemical cyclicals, the stock is expensive at 32.6x against a 5-8x mid-cycle norm, and 83.7x trailing P/E, 42.1x forward P/E and 4.4x P/B on just 5.8% ROE support that view, though the peer ranks (P89 on trailing P/E) use a broad-market fallback rather than close peers, and the 12% dividend yield and 40.34 debt/equity look unreliable, so I did not rely on them. The biggest risk is that the price already assumes a sharp earnings ramp, with next-year estimates up 21.9% over 90 days while current-year estimates fell 22.1%, so a weak result could trigger a de-rating, especially as FY26 free cash flow was Rs -221 cr and October filings show promoter encumbrance disclosures whose details were not provided.

fundamental.thesis: J.K. Cement is a mid-sized cement maker that is also building a paints business through its subsidiary JK Maxx Paints. fundamental.thesis: NMDC Steel is a government-controlled (50.79% GoI stake) integrated steel producer demerged from NMDC Ltd, operating a greenfield Nagarnar plant and currently awaiting a strategic disinvestment buyer — creating a persistent ownership overhang. Q1FY27 revenue grew 8.8% YoY to ₹3,662cr, a sharp deceleration from +72.4% in 9MFY26 and +178.9% in FY25, but the critical directional story is the margin turnaround: PAT margin has expanded from −35.8% (Q3FY25) through −3.4% (9MFY26) to +1.4% (Q1FY27) as the greenfield plant ramps utilisation and fixed-cost absorption improves. Using EV/EBITDA — the correct yardstick for a capital-intensive steel cyclical — NSLNISP trades at 11.69× versus the broad-market median of 23.3×, placing it at P17 (cheap), and P/B of 1.05× puts it at P3; the 235× trailing P/E is a pure distortion of near-zero earnings and must not be read as 'expensive', but D/E of 35× and a DSCR of only 0.17 mean the company cannot comfortably service its own debt and any spread compression could tip it back to losses. The single biggest risk is that extreme financial leverage leaves no margin of safety against rising crude costs (a direct input-cost headwind in the current macro), a weakening rupee, and the prolonged disinvestment uncertainty that suppresses any rerating.

Premier Energies makes solar cells and modules and, since buying 51% of Transcon in April 2026, also has a power transmission and distribution equipment business. Q2 FY27 figures, derived by subtracting Q1 from H1, show revenue of about Rs 2,631 cr (+43.2% YoY, up from +35.2% in Q1) and PAT of about Rs 462 cr (+31.0%, down from +53.3%), while EBITDA margin fell from 35.1% to about 28.8% YoY; growth was about +20% in FY26 before the deal, and organic growth is not disclosed in the data provided, so the acceleration may be largely acquired, and the 'expanding' PAT margin signal is unreliable because it rests on a likely erroneous Q1 FY26 revenue figure of Rs 182 cr, with PAT margin actually slipping from 19.1% in Q1 to about 17.6% in Q2. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for a capital-intensive business, 20.5x is about 12% below the broad-market median (P44), and trailing P/E of 31.4x sits inside the 28-45x sector range, so valuation is fair, though the peer set is not a close comparison, order-book data needed for the sector card's framework is missing, and the 14.0% dividend yield and the +26% upside to the consensus target look unreliable (market cap and 52-week position suggest a price nearer Rs 1,057, or only about 5% upside). The biggest risk is funding: H1 free cash flow was Rs -733 cr, with operating cash flow of Rs 669 cr against capex of Rs 1,402 cr, before the newly approved Rs 5,947 cr ingot and wafer project, while margins are falling and Rs 2,422 cr of Transcon goodwill is on the balance sheet.

fundamental.thesis: Nuvoco Vistas is an East- and North-focused cement and ready-mix concrete (RMC) maker with about 35 MTPA of target capacity. It is a mid-tier player in a sector where UltraTech and Adani now control about 45% of capacity. Using the filings trend table (the yfinance rows are inconsistent and were ignored), Q2FY27 revenue rose 13.5% YoY to ₹2,790 cr, up from +9.0% in Q1, and cement volumes grew 9% YoY against 5% in Q1. Profit quality is thinner than the headline suggests. PAT rose 78% YoY, but only to ₹65 cr, a 2.3% margin. EBITDA margin fell to 14.7% from 18.3% in Q1 and 15.1% a year ago. Implied EBITDA per tonne is about ₹875, below the healthy ₹900–1,100 band and down from roughly ₹1,080 in Q1. Valuation is graded on EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a capital-intensive cement maker, not P/E. At 8.6x (P8 of the broad market, no close peers in the universe), with P/B of 1.09x, forward P/E of 20.5x against trailing 31x, and the price at 18% of its 52-week range, the stock looks cheap against typical cement multiples. Much of that discount is justified by an ROE of only 3.7% and high debt. The biggest risk is the balance sheet. Net debt is ₹5,028 cr, current ratio is 0.57x, free cash flow was -₹246 cr in H1 because of capex, and legal disputes are pending: the ₹490 cr CCI penalty and about ₹454 cr of West Bengal incentive provisions. These come on top of rising crude and a weak rupee pushing up fuel and freight costs.

fundamental.thesis: SRF is a diversified Indian chemicals and packaging-films maker; most of its profit comes from refrigerant gases and specialty chemicals for agrochemical and pharma clients. The SECTOR CARD places it in specialty chemicals, with the ref-gas cycle turning up. The latest quarter in the official trend table is Q1FY27, which showed revenue of ₹5,033 cr (+31.8% YoY) and PAT of ₹759 cr (+75.5% YoY), with EBITDA margin rising to 25.2% from about 18-20% through 9MFY26 and FY26 (FY26 revenue grew only +7.5%, so growth has re-accelerated sharply). However, the Q2FY27 results filed on 21 Oct are not yet in the extracted table, the yfinance Q2 revenue of ₹2,600 cr looks inconsistent with that run-rate (likely standalone or partial), and the H1FY26 row appears mislabelled, so the newest quarter is unverified. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the card names for chemical cyclicals: 19.2x EV/EBITDA, 34.6x trailing P/E and 27.9x forward P/E sit well above the card's 5-8x mid-cycle EV/EBITDA and the 12-22x Materials P/E band, so it grades expensive. The 'cheap vs peers' verdict is not usable because the peer set is capital-goods names (ABB, CGPOWER, HAL) after a yfinance Industrials mis-tag; the stock sitting near its 52-week low (19% of range) only partly offsets this. The biggest risk is earnings quality and cycle dependence: H1 cash conversion was weak (CFO/PAT 0.63x, FCF -₹180 cr) during a heavy capex phase (₹974 cr in H1), with ₹165 cr of forex losses, so any cooling in refrigerant-gas pricing would hit a peak-margin earnings base.

fundamental.thesis: Indian Overseas Bank is a mid-sized public sector lender with advances of about Rs 3.46 lakh crore, growing well above the roughly 16% FY26 sector credit growth in the sector card at +24.35% YoY. In Q2FY27, revenue growth decelerated from +23.3% to +13.2% YoY (Rs 10,428 cr), while PAT growth accelerated from +45.7% to +56.0% (Rs 1,912 cr), helped by NIM of 3.49% vs 3.35% in FY26, gross NPA of 1.19% vs 1.83% in H1FY26, and credit cost of 0.17%; the pre-computed 'accelerating' revenue signal is unreliable because it reads newest-to-oldest across mixed periods and FY26 revenue (Rs 17,900 cr) is below H1FY26 (Rs 18,084 cr). Using P/B plus ROE, the right yardstick for a lender, valuation is fair: P/B of 1.63x sits just above the 1.5x cheap threshold despite 16.5% TTM ROE (the bank reports 24.58%), trailing P/E of 11.03x is not the basis for the grade, the 'cheap vs peers' rank is against the broad market rather than banks, and the 36.51x forward P/E conflicts with recent earnings and needs checking, though being 15.7% up the 52-week range offers a better entry point. The biggest risk is that profit growth depends on unusually low credit costs while loans grow rapidly, with non-interest income down 10.11% YoY, CRAR down to 18.60% from 19.36% in a quarter, and a CFO change effective 01.11.2026 adding a governance item to monitor.

Deepak Nitrite is an integrated Indian chemicals maker with a leading position in phenol and acetone (Phenolics), plus an Advanced Intermediates (AI) business serving agrochemical and other customers. Quarterly revenue growth has accelerated from +3.0% in Q3 FY26 and -3.0% in Q4 to +36.4% in Q1 FY27 and about +62% in Q2, while H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 5,654 cr (+49.0%) and PAT Rs 743 cr (+222%); Q2 is derived as H1 minus Q1 (revenue about Rs 3,076 cr, PAT about Rs 398 cr, margin about 12.9% vs 13.4% in Q1), and the gain leans on Phenolics, with H1 EBIT of Rs 933 cr, while AI margin fell to 7% from 10%. Using EV/EBITDA, the sector card's yardstick for chemical cyclicals, I grade valuation fair: the 24.6x headline (+37% vs the 17.9x peer median, P67) and 41.6x trailing P/E appear to use FY26 earnings, and my rough trailing-12-month estimates are about 14x EV/EBITDA and 22x P/E, which is below the headline but still above the card's 5-8x mid-cycle range on what may be peak earnings, while the 27.6x forward P/E implies PAT of only about Rs 830 cr, so either that figure is stale or earnings are expected to fall despite upward EPS revisions (the snapshot's dividend yield and implied price also look unreliable). The biggest risk is that Phenolics spreads normalise, as management itself signals with its 'new normal' language, just as the long-dated polycarbonate project (FY27 capex plan Rs 2,500 cr vs FY26 FCF of Rs 348 cr, commercialisation targeted by end FY2030) adds debt without near-term earnings.

fundamental.thesis: Chennai Petroleum is a standalone refiner and IOC subsidiary, so its earnings track gross refining margins (GRM, the profit per barrel of crude processed) rather than administered retail fuel prices. Taking the official H1FY27 filing (₹51,414 cr revenue, ₹3,278 cr PAT) and subtracting Q1 gives an implied Q2FY27 revenue of about ₹22,055 cr, up roughly 10% YoY. That is a sharp slowdown from +57% in Q1, so the pre-computed 'accelerating' label is misleading because it mixes half-year and quarterly periods. Implied Q2 PAT was ₹2,247 cr, a 10.2% margin, driven by GRM rising to $8.78/bbl from $3.22 a year ago and a ₹385 cr one-off retrospective price adjustment, even though crude throughput fell 4.5%. On live ratios the stock looks cheap, using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for a capital-intensive refiner: trailing P/E 5.4x, EV/EBITDA 3.8x and P/B 1.5x against a 32% ROE, all bottom-percentile versus the market and below the 8–14x energy band. However, these are peak-cycle refining margins, and next-year EPS estimates were cut 11.6% in the last 30 days, so normalised earnings likely put it closer to fair. The bigger worry is earnings quality: H1 operating cash flow was only ₹25 cr against ₹3,278 cr of profit (0.01x), receivables jumped from ₹235 cr to ₹2,008 cr, cash fell to near zero after dividends, and the auditor flagged board-composition non-compliance.

fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Finance is India's largest diversified retail NBFC, with AUM of ₹5,84,624 cr and a customer franchise of 128.85 million. In Q2FY27, net total income grew 23% YoY to ₹15,974 cr and PAT grew 29% to ₹6,367 cr, while AUM growth picked up from 22.4% (Q4FY26) to 24% (Q1) to 26%, and GNPA improved to 1.06% from 1.24% a year ago. Note that the trend table's Q1FY27 and H1 'revenue' rows appear to use total income rather than net income, so I rely on the like-for-like Q2 net-income figures. Using the sector card's lender yardstick of P/B against ROE, the stock trades at 4.93x book for a 17.9% TTM ROE (20.6% annualised in Q2), the most expensive P/B among its 10 credit-services peers (P100, +62% vs the 3.0x median) and P89 on P/E at 29.6x, so it is expensive even after allowing a quality premium. The 18.3x forward P/E and the 62% dividend yield look like data errors and are not relied on. The biggest risk is that management itself guides to modest NIM moderation with up to two more repo hikes to 6%, which turns the NBFC rate tailwind into a headwind. Stage 2 and 3 assets have also risen to 2.02% from 1.87%, and the ₹17,500 cr QIP plus promoter warrants will dilute ROE in the near term.

Revenue growth accelerated from +9.8% in Q1 to +20.6% (₹54,486 cr), and PAT rose 225.6% to ₹5,359 cr, though the YoY figures use a low, restructured base; PAT margin was flat at about 9.8-9.9%, the 'contracting' signal is distorted by FY26's ₹18,051 cr one-off gain, and EBITDA per tonne fell about 11% QoQ from ₹14,990 to ₹13,329 despite rising 24% YoY. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a steel cyclical, the stock is expensive: the reported 12.6x, or roughly 9x on my estimate using annualised Q2 EBITDA and net debt, is above the 5-8x mid-cycle norm, and the 13.8x trailing P/E and 'cheap vs peers' verdict carry little weight because of the one-off gain and a peer set that includes paint and adhesive companies. The biggest risk is that steel spreads narrow from here, with the stock at 92% of its 52-week range and EBITDA per tonne already falling sequentially, leaving little room for error.

Sun Pharma is India's largest drugmaker, with an 8.6% domestic market share (up 0.3pp), a growing innovative medicines business (21.5% of sales) and a pending USD 14.0 bn purchase of Organon. Q2FY27 revenue growth was +11.8% (H1 ₹31,499 cr, +11.0%), slower than the +15.1% in the 9MFY26 row but steady over recent periods, with India up 16.6% in H1 offsetting an 8.2% Q2 fall in US sales; H1 PAT fell 9.5% to ₹4,883 cr, implying Q2 PAT of about ₹1,988 cr (roughly -36% YoY) after exceptional charges, while adjusted PAT grew only 2.2% and EBITDA margin was about 29%, down from 31.9%. On trailing P/E of 37.4x (near the top of the 28-40x pharma range, P54 vs peers) and EV/EBITDA of 24.2x (P62, 13% above the peer median), the grade is fair, not cheap, and the 27.7x forward P/E relies on estimates that have been cut 2.9% over the past 30 days and 3.4% over 90 days despite 29 of 34 analysts rating it a buy. The biggest risk is that Organon's costs and funding weigh on earnings and turn the ₹17,675 cr net cash position into debt while US sales are shrinking; conviction is held down by data errors in this pack, as the extracted exceptional charges (₹14,729 cr) and adjusted PAT (₹62,515 cr) are not plausible against reported figures, the FY26 and 9MFY26 rows look misscaled, and the feed's 5.52 debt/equity and 93% dividend yield look wrong, so none of these absolute figures were relied on.

NTPC is India's largest power generator, earning mainly a regulated return on its expanding asset base, with solar a small but fast-growing addition (H1 solar revenue +64.9% to ₹2,456 cr). Revenue growth has improved from about -0.4% in FY26 to +7.0% in Q1 FY27 and +9.65% in H1 FY27 on a like-for-like capacity-plus-energy basis (₹91,754 cr vs ₹83,660 cr), but the +19.9% headline is overstated because it compares a broader revenue estimate with that narrower base; capacity charges, the best proxy for regulated earnings, grew a steadier +6.7%, while H1 PAT was not extracted, Q1 PAT rose 12.9% to ₹6,896 cr at a 13.6% margin, and the table's 'expanding' margin signals are unreliable because they mix cumulative periods of different lengths. Using EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick for a capital-intensive utility, valuation looks cheap at 8.36× vs a peer median of 11.6× (cheapest of 5), with trailing P/E of 11.9× also the lowest among peers and at the low end of the 10-18× sector range, though the Adani names inflate the peer medians, forward P/E of 12.81× is above trailing, and FY26 profit may be flattered because it implies about ₹13,131 cr in Q4 alone, so this is a moderate rather than deep discount. The biggest risk is earnings quality and regulation: CERC 2024 tariff orders are still pending, so billing remains provisional with retrospective adjustments, and the sell-side +32% upside should be discounted because a ₹3.5L cr market cap and the 48.5% 52-week range position imply a price near ₹360, or about +16% to the ₹419 target.

fundamental.thesis: Eicher Motors is India's dominant mid-weight motorcycle manufacturer through Royal Enfield (87% domestic market share in the segment) with an expanding global footprint and a 50:50 JV in VECV (commercial vehicles), giving it a structurally premium and defensible franchise. Q1FY27 revenue surged 31.6% YoY to ₹6,632 cr with PAT up 21.4% to ₹1,463 cr — however, PAT margin compressed 181 bps YoY to 22.0%, and the PAT growth meaningfully lagging revenue growth signals cost absorption headwinds despite strong volumes; the EBITDA margin trend is more encouraging, expanding to 31.0% in Q1FY27 from ~24–25% in mid-FY26, suggesting operating leverage is materialising at the gross level even as below-the-line costs (finance, depreciation from capex ramp) create PAT drag. On the sector-preferred P/E yardstick, trailing P/E of 37.9× sits at the P80 peer percentile and commands a 40% premium to the sector median of 27.1×; EV/EBITDA at 33.7× is P100 in its peer set and 84% above the sector median — on both measures the stock is expensive relative to peers, and the forward P/E of 28.8× (still P83) reflects already-priced-in earnings growth, leaving limited re-rating room. The key risk is the combination of a RISK_OFF macro (FII selling, rising crude costs for consumers, Auto sector underweight tilt) with a stock already in the top quartile of peer valuations and PAT margins visibly compressing — any festive season demand disappointment or further input cost spike would catalyse a derating without a valuation cushion.

fundamental.thesis: Adani Power is India's largest private thermal generator (18.3 GW operating, 23.7 GW under construction), with about 88-95% of capacity tied to long-term PPAs and the rest sold on the merchant market, which makes it a power-cycle business rather than a regulated annuity like NTPC or POWERGRID. fundamental.thesis: Canara Bank is a large public sector bank (62.93% GoI ownership) and one of India's top-5 lenders by advances (₹13.6L cr), with a franchise spanning retail, wholesale, and treasury segments; the key yardstick here is P/B vs ROE, per the sector card, not P/E. H1FY27 shows a notable bifurcation: PAT grew strongly +31.3% YoY to ₹10,562 cr on dramatically improved asset quality (Gross NPA 1.33%, Net NPA 0.30%, PCR 95.34%), but total income contracted -3.38% YoY — revenue trajectory has decelerated from +7.7% (FY26) to -3.4% (H1FY27), driven by treasury revenue declining -18% YoY and NIM compression (2.06% FY26 vs 2.51% in Q4FY26), while PAT margin has expanded from 11.7% (FY26) to 13.1% (H1FY27) on sharply lower credit costs. At P/B of 1.02× against ROE of 15.9%, the stock is unambiguously cheap by the sector card's prescribed lender yardstick — sector card benchmark is P/B < 1.5 with ROE > 12% = cheap — and sits at P0 (cheapest) in its 14-peer regional bank cohort on both trailing P/E (6.1×, -64% vs median 16.8×) and forward P/E (5.7×), though much of this structural discount is explained by PSU overhang and below-median CASA (29.86% vs private sector ~40%+). The single biggest risk is NIM pressure persisting through the deposit repricing cycle — NIM at 2.06% for FY26 is already thin for a PSU bank and any further compression from EBLR-linked loan repricing faster than deposit cost decline would erode the PAT margin expansion thesis and keep revenue growth negative.

DOMS Industries is a branded stationery and art-materials maker with a smaller, faster-growing hygiene segment; H1 FY27 segment growth was 18.0% and 22.5% respectively, though its market position cannot be established from this data. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.6% YoY to Rs 667.75 cr, continuing a slowdown from +26.4% in Q1 FY26, while PAT fell 37.0% to Rs 38.32 cr, the PAT margin dropped from 10.7% to 5.7%, and H1 EBITDA margin was 12.2% against 17.3% in FY26 (the trend table's Rs 67,051 cr Q1 FY27 revenue is a unit error, and H1 figures imply about Rs 670 cr). Using the FMCG card's P/E norm of 40-65x as the main yardstick, 59.4x trailing P/E is within the band but near its top, and I grade it expensive because earnings are falling, it ranks P78 on P/E against a broad-market peer set with no close comparables, EV/EBITDA is 33.3x, and the 40.5x forward P/E relies on estimates already cut 16.1% for the current year in 30 days; being only 13.3% above the 52-week low does not by itself make it good value. The biggest risk is that the margin drop proves structural rather than temporary, as the filings data here does not explain the cause, while H1 free cash flow was Rs -106 cr with capex at 15.7% of revenue and the Company Secretary resigned on results day.

fundamental.thesis: Indian Hotels (IHCL) runs India's largest hotel chain, with Taj and other brands across 670 hotels including 280 in the pipeline. It earns more and more from asset-light management fees, which grew 25% YoY in Q2, and it is still early in a RevPAR (revenue per available room) upcycle, up 25% YoY in Q2 and 28% for full-service hotels. Q2FY27 revenue rose 21.0% YoY to ₹2,566 cr, up from +14.6% in Q1FY27. PAT rose 23.0% to ₹349 cr. Management raised full-year revenue guidance from 12-14% to 15-17%, and H1 cash conversion was strong (CFO/PAT 1.27x, FCF ₹546 cr). The 'contracting' margin signal mostly reflects comparing a seasonally weak Q2 against full-year figures: on a same-quarter basis the EBITDA margin (30.7%) and PAT margin (13.6%) are roughly flat to slightly up YoY. On valuation, hotels are capital-intensive, so I used EV/EBITDA as the main yardstick. At 28.2x, IHCL sits around the 61st percentile of its sector, with a trailing P/E of 44.5x (P59) and a forward P/E of 35.6x. That is fair, not cheap, for 20%+ earnings growth, and the stock sits at 38.5% of its 52-week range. Note that the snapshot's 49% dividend yield and 18.99 debt/equity look like data-unit errors, given ₹4,369 cr of gross cash. The biggest risk is that a premium-multiple discretionary stock gets de-rated in a risk-off market with crude above $100, which could squeeze travel and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences and events) demand even while operating numbers stay strong.

C.E. Info Systems (MapmyIndia) sells digital maps, location data and related devices, and is a small mid-cap valued at about Rs 5,070 cr. H1 FY27 revenue rose 15.3% YoY to Rs 271 cr, up from about +2.3% in FY26, and PAT rose 32.1% to Rs 85 cr; Q2 derived from H1 less Q1 shows revenue of about Rs 131 cr (about +16% YoY) and PAT of about Rs 35 cr (about +90% off a low Rs 18.5 cr base), but both fell from Q1's Rs 140 cr and Rs 50 cr. The acceleration is low quality because devices grew 161% to Rs 56 cr and supplied nearly all the added revenue, while core map data and services (79% of revenue) grew just 0.66%. Using IT-sector P/E plus EV/EBITDA, valuation is fair rather than cheap despite the stock sitting near its 52-week low: trailing P/E of 36.9x is above the 22-30x IT range, while forward P/E of 22.5x and EV/EBITDA of 29.1x (P64) sit around or above the broad-market median, though no close peers exist and the forward multiple needs earnings growth that a flat core may not deliver; the biggest risk is that core stagnation persists while near-term estimates drift lower (next-FY EPS -2.1% over 30 days).

fundamental.thesis: Marico is a domestic hair-oil and edible-oil franchise (Parachute, Saffola) with growing foods, digital-first brands and international businesses; about 96% of the business was gaining or holding market share in Q1 FY27. Q1 FY27 was strong and volume-led, with revenue up 19.9% to Rs 3,957 cr, India volume growth of 11% and EBITDA margin up 40 bps to 20.7%, but Q2 FY27 is unverified: the extracted revenue of Rs 2,722 cr (+8.4%) and PAT of Rs 683 cr (+71.6%, or Rs 550 cr attributable to the parent) look like mixed reporting bases and include unitemised exceptional items, so neither the apparent slowdown nor the 25.1% margin should be trusted. Using trailing P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers as the yardstick, the stock is expensive: its 59.4x P/E is near the top of the 40-65x FMCG norm and 35.5% above the 43.8x peer median, while its 44.1x EV/EBITDA is 42.2% above the 31.0x median, and it sits at about 80% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that a premium multiple is being paid for growth the latest quarter cannot yet confirm, particularly as the 11% volume growth is above the roughly 10% level the sector card treats sceptically and rising crude could pressure input costs.

fundamental.thesis: HDFC AMC is one of India's top-two mutual fund managers, with about 13% QAAUM market share, roughly ₹9.3 lakh cr of QAAUM and around ₹6 lakh cr in equity AUM. It runs an asset-light, debt-free model whose earnings move with equity AUM and SIP flows; its retail franchise is strong, with 16.7M unique investors and SIP/STP flows of about ₹4,880 cr a month, up 33% YoY. The latest quarter we have read is Q1 FY27: revenue rose 13.6% YoY to ₹1,100 cr and PAT rose 12.0% to ₹837 cr. That is a slowdown from FY26, when revenue grew +17.8% to ₹4,122 cr and PAT grew +16.2% to ₹2,858 cr. The 'accelerating' revenue signal in the trend table reads the series in the wrong order, and two of its rows (Q4FY26 ₹41 cr, 9MFY26) have broken units, so we ignored them. One important caveat: the Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-10-15 have not been read, so all figures here are one quarter stale. We graded valuation on earnings multiples suited to an AMC, as the sector card says, not on P/B against lenders. On that basis it is fair: 35.5x trailing and 27.4x forward P/E for a debt-free business with ROA around 29% and a payout near 80%. The 'expensive vs peers' tag and P/B of 11x compare it with banks and NBFCs, which is the wrong peer set, and the snapshot's 222% dividend yield and 2.36 debt/equity are data errors for a debt-free AMC. The stock sits at 26% of its 52-week range, which is a reasonable entry point. Against that, sell-side EPS estimates are being cut steadily (-1.4% over 30 days, -2.0% over 90 days) even though 25 of 27 analysts rate it Buy, which points to a slower earnings path ahead.

Lupin is a US-heavy generics maker, ranked 3rd in US prescriptions, with a large India branded business (8th in India; chronic therapies growing 19.5% in H1 vs 17.2% for the market). Q2 FY27 revenue growth slowed to about +14% (roughly Rs 7,800 cr; the trend table's Rs 779 cr looks like a scale error) from +32.1% in Q1, and revenue fell from Rs 8,277 cr in Q1, while Q2 PAT of about Rs 1,160-1,186 cr fell 22-25% YoY after +5.1% in Q1, with PAT margin at about 14.8% vs 19.1% in FY26 and EBITDA margin at 25.1% vs about 34% implied for Q1, partly due to a higher tax rate (26.7% vs 13.4% in H1) and the VISUfarma deal also adding non-organic revenue. Using EV/EBITDA and P/E against peers, the valuation is cheap: EV/EBITDA of 12.4x is at P8 vs a 21.4x median and trailing P/E of 19.4x is at P0 vs 36.4x, but the discount is less convincing than it looks because trailing earnings include a peak FY26 (PAT +62%), forward P/E of 22.1x is higher than trailing and only modestly below peers (P23), and the snapshot's 52-week position conflicts with the price implied by the consensus target, so we place no weight on it. The biggest risk is that the Q2 margin drop proves lasting rather than one-off, with FY EPS estimates already cut 5.5% over 90 days, though the balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA 0.44x, H1 CFO/PAT 1.12x) gives it room to absorb this; the 29.39 debt/equity reading appears to be a percentage (about 0.29x), not high leverage.

fundamental.thesis: Laurus Labs is a vertically integrated API and CDMO business with a dominant ARV generics franchise (41% of FY26 revenue) and a rapidly scaling CDMO segment (30%+ of FY26 revenue, targeting 50% by FY30) supported by 8,200 kl reactor capacity, 110 active CDMO pipeline projects, and zero critical audit findings across 132 inspections — a credible China+1 CDMO beneficiary. FY26 revenue grew +23% YoY to ₹6,813 cr with PAT up +148% YoY to ₹890 cr (PAT margin 13.1%); CDMO small-molecule delivered +38% growth and 9M CDMO grew +50%, though full-year revenue growth decelerated modestly from the +30% pace seen in 9MFY26 to +23% for the full year, while EBITDA margins expanded to 26.8% with very strong cash conversion (CFO/PAT 1.82x FY26). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive CDMO/API model, the stock trades at 52.5x vs a sector median of 21.4x — a 145% premium — and ranks P100 (most expensive) across trailing P/E (96.6x), forward P/E (67.2x), P/B (19.8x), and EV/EBITDA in its 14-stock peer group, with the stock at 99.1% of its 52-week range: unambiguously expensive even granting a deserved CDMO re-rating premium. A ₹3,000 cr capex programme (nearly 3× the prior ₹1,000 cr guidance) must convert to contracted CDMO revenue without material slippage while the stock prices in near-flawless execution, with a pending US generics tariff review and inherent CDMO quarter-to-quarter lumpiness creating headline risk at this multiple.

fundamental.thesis: ICICI Prudential AMC is India's largest listed asset management company, earning fee income on equity and debt AUM; it is a pure-beta play on India's financialisation theme (AUM growth +25.6% YoY as of Q4FY26) with an asset-light model generating 85.8% ROE. Revenue growth has decelerated from +23.5% (Q3FY26) to +16.9% (H1FY27, ₹3,238 cr) while PAT growth slowed to +14.3% YoY (₹1,854 cr); PAT margin at 57.2% in H1FY27 has compressed from the 60–61% range seen earlier, and EBITDA margins are on a contracting trajectory — the direction of change is negative even if absolute levels remain high. Using the sector-card mandated P/AUM-linked earnings yardstick, the stock trades at 51.33× trailing P/E and 35.11× EV/EBITDA (P74 vs broad market peers, +50% premium to median), with forward P/E of 36.77× implying priced-in earnings recovery — graded fair given the ROE-justified premium, but the stock at 83% of its 52-week range with consistently negative estimate revisions (FY-EPS cut –5.8% in 30d, next-FY cut –10.5% in 90d) provides very limited margin of safety. The biggest risk is a classic pre-derating setup: sell-side estimates being quietly cut while ratings remain bullish and the pending PMS acquisition from ICICI Securities adds regulatory and integration overhang.

IEX runs India's power exchange, an asset-light platform that earns mostly transaction fees, and real-time market volumes have grown to 41% of electricity volumes in H1 FY27 from 20% in FY23. Q2 FY27 total income rose 10.8% YoY to Rs 203 cr and PAT rose 12.9% to Rs 139 cr, but growth has slowed from +19.3% in Q1 FY26, and the table's 'expanding' margin signal is largely a mismatch between total-income and operating-revenue figures: on total income, PAT margin was steadier at about 65.5%, 67.3%, 66.4% and 68.5% over the comparable quarters, while Q2 operating revenue growth was only about +8% by my derivation from the H1 and Q1 figures. The sector card's lender yardstick does not fit an exchange, so I graded on P/E and EV/EBITDA: 22.3x trailing P/E and 14.2x EV/EBITDA sit at P26 and P24 of a broad-market peer set, not true exchange peers, and near the 52-week low, which I read as fair rather than cheap given the regulatory overhang, next-year EPS estimates cut 5.5% over 90 days and about Rs 45 cr of quarterly other income flattering PAT. I disregarded the 324% dividend yield and 0.82 debt/equity as suspect, and the +18.5% consensus upside because it implies a price near Rs 112, below the Rs 115 52-week low; the biggest risk is that market coupling redistributes IEX's market share, while H1 CFO/PAT of 0.73x also needs watching.

fundamental.thesis: Dr Reddy's is a large Indian generics maker with heavy US exposure, plus a fast-growing India branded business and emerging-market and biosimilar franchises. The latest quarter extracted from filings is Q1 FY27; Q2 FY27 results were filed on 23 Oct but not yet extracted, and the yfinance Q2 revenue of 4,150 cr is about half the normal run-rate, so it is treated as suspect. In Q1 FY27 revenue fell 5.6% YoY to 8,070 cr, down from +3.0% in FY26, and PAT fell 69% to 435 cr (5.4% margin, down from 12.8%), partly because of a 223 cr semaglutide inventory provision. Even after stripping that one-off, US revenue fell 35% while India formulations grew a healthy 17%, and cash conversion was very weak (CFO/PAT 0.23x, FCF of -22 cr). On valuation I used P/E and EV/EBITDA against peers: trailing P/E of 24.8x sits below the 28-40x sector band and at P23 among peers, with forward P/E (19.8x) and P/B (2.8x) both at P8, so the grade is cheap. That discount partly reflects a depressed, declining earnings base, an ROE of only 11.8%, and analyst estimates that have been cut slightly over 30 and 90 days. The biggest risk is that the US generics decline and the semaglutide delay keep hitting earnings before new launches can fill the gap.

fundamental.thesis: Infosys is India's second-largest IT services exporter, a debt-free, cash-generative tier-1 franchise now caught in the sector's AI reset, where productivity gains are shrinking legacy time-and-materials revenue. On P/EV, the right yardstick for a life insurer, LICI looks cheap at about 0.63x (₹5.0L cr market cap against ₹7,97,378 cr embedded value), and its 8.71x trailing P/E and 2.05x P/B are also the lowest among life peers, though those two measures are only weak support and peer P/EV was not provided. The biggest risk is that margin-led profit growth fades, given embedded value fell 1.95%, policies sold fell 2.25%, individual non-par APE fell 5.98%, and operating cash flow was -₹16,746 cr (-0.65x PAT), which management attributes to timing.

fundamental.thesis: APL Apollo Tubes is India's largest structural steel tube maker, reporting about 65% market share, and runs a branded, near-zero working capital model with net cash of Rs 1,600 cr. The Q2FY27 row is blank, so subtracting Q1 from H1 implies revenue of about Rs 7,001 cr (+26.6% YoY, up from +8.4% in Q1) and PAT of about Rs 383 cr (+26.8%, up from +10.9%), with PAT margin improving from 4.7% to about 5.5% on record volume of 960k tons and EBITDA per ton rising from Rs 5,500 in Q4FY26 to Rs 6,000; the pre-computed trajectory signals were not relied on because they mix period types and the Q3FY26 and Q4FY26 figures look wrong. fundamental.thesis: Godrej Properties is an asset-light residential developer that has doubled its national market share from 2.4% in CY21 to 4.8% in CY25. Its FY26 operating base looks healthy: bookings were ₹34,171 cr (+16% YoY), collections ₹19,965 cr (+17%) and new project additions ₹42,100 cr (+59%). Reported H1 FY27 numbers are weaker: revenue rose 107.8% YoY to ₹2,441 cr, but PAT fell 49.8% to ₹495 cr (12.6% margin). That PAT includes a ₹309 cr non-cash fair-value gain, so underlying profit is roughly ₹186 cr. Operating cash flow was negative at ₹-724 cr, and net debt rose from ₹7,607 cr in Q1 to ₹8,111 cr. The trend table mixes quarterly, half-year and full-year periods, so the 'accelerating' and 'contracting' labels are not reliable, and H1 FY27 bookings and collections are not in the data, which leaves a gap in the metrics that matter most here. I graded valuation on enterprise value to pre-sales (bookings) and P/B against ROE, not P/E, because reported profit here lags actual sales by 2–4 years. Enterprise value is about ₹59,500 cr, or roughly 1.7× FY26 bookings. P/B is 2.68× against ROE of 10%, and the stock sits at 25% of its 52-week range, so it looks fair, leaning slightly cheap. The biggest risk is that cash generation weakens while debt rises in a risk-off market.

fundamental.thesis: 360 ONE WAM is India's leading listed wealth and asset management platform, serving ~8,900 UHNI/HNI client families across total AUM of ₹7.77 lakh crore, with 75% of revenue sourced from recurring ARR fees at a steady 74 bps retention — an asset-light, sticky-fee franchise with a strong track record of near-zero NPA on its Lombard lending book since 2016. H1FY27 revenue grew +14.7% YoY to ₹2,367 cr, decelerating sharply from +28.8% in Q2FY26, while PAT grew only +5.1% YoY to ₹631 cr as PAT margin compressed from 39.0% (FY26) to 24.9% — the headline pain from a 25.7% YoY decline in Wealth Management segment PBT, partially offset by Asset Management revenue surging +65.7% YoY; ARR AUM for Wealth Management nonetheless grew +24.2% YoY, signalling the underlying fee base is intact even as near-term PBT is under pressure from rising employee costs (+28.7% YoY). Using EV/EBITDA (the sector card's prescribed yardstick for AMC; P/E is unreliable here) at 21.4x — an 8.2% discount to the peer median of 23.3x and at the P46 percentile — alongside a forward P/E of 27.45x vs trailing 39.18x implying the street prices in a meaningful earnings recovery, and P/B 4.71x on tangible ROE 19.4%, the stock grades as fairly valued with a slight EV/EBITDA lean toward cheap. The key risk is that Wealth Management PBT decline proves structural — if the rapid lending book expansion (67.8% YoY, driving deeply negative operating cash flows of -₹724 cr in H1FY27) permanently shifts the business mix away from the asset-light advisory model and the IT tax assessment (₹336 cr under appeal) crystallises, the premium multiple is vulnerable to a derating.

H1 PAT fell 8.9% to Rs 1,116 cr, PAT margin dropped from 19.35% to 15.94%, and EBITDA fell 11.4% to a 20.7% margin, with Q2 PAT and margin not separately available. On EV/EBITDA, the main yardstick for this business, the stock looks expensive at 50.3x versus a 34.0x peer median (P71, trailing P/E 67.7x at P56), near the top of its 52-week range, and the biggest risk is a de-rating if margins and estimates keep falling (FY EPS estimates down 6.0% over 90 days).

fundamental.thesis: Bharat Forge is a global forging and auto-components maker with a fast-growing Indian defence arm, so it should be judged on the US and EU truck and auto cycles and on defence delivery, not on Indian auto demand alone. fundamental.thesis: Bajaj Housing Finance is a large housing-finance NBFC in the Bajaj group, lending to home buyers, property owners and developers, with AUM up 25% YoY to ₹1,58,205 cr and asset quality that remains very clean (GNPA 0.29%, NNPA 0.12%). PAT was about ₹757 cr, up about 17.7% YoY, and PAT margin has held flat near 23%. Under the surface, net interest income grew only 9.8% YoY against 24-25% loan growth, NIM slipped from 3.5% to 3.36%, credit cost rose to 0.52% in Q1FY27 from 0.15% in FY26, and capital adequacy fell from 26.1% to 21.2% as the book grew faster than equity. The biggest risk is that loan growth keeps outrunning lending spreads and capital, while the CFO's resignation on 2026-10-23 adds governance and continuity uncertainty for a midcap lender running debt-to-equity near 4.9x.

fundamental.thesis: Can Fin Homes is a mid-size Housing Finance Company (HFC) and Canara Bank subsidiary, focused on affordable housing (83% of portfolio) across 21 states through 250 branches — a niche lender with institutional parentage and a structurally low-cost origination model. PAT growth has re-accelerated from -4.3% YoY in Q1FY26 through +18% in Q2FY26 and +27% in FY26, sustaining at +20.2% in Q1FY27 (₹268 cr); H1FY27 PAT margin expanded to 24.4% from 22.4% in Q1FY26, and GNPA collapsed from 6.71% (Q1FY26) to 0.90% (H1FY27) while disbursement growth surged to 29% YoY in Q1FY27 — a leading signal for portfolio acceleration — though NIM has edged down from 3.93% (FY26) to 3.81% (Q1FY27), using the sector-card P/B+ROE yardstick for lenders, P/B of 1.74× against ROE of 17.15% grades clearly cheap (below the 1.5× threshold but with materially above-12% ROE), with the stock sitting at P5 in broad-market peers, near its 52-week low, and forward P/E of 8.23× below trailing 9.19× confirming further earnings growth priced in. The biggest risk to this thesis is NIM erosion accelerating: deposit repricing typically lags EBLR-linked asset yield cuts in an easing cycle, the LCR has already fallen from 250% in Q1FY27 to 100% at H1FY27 (the regulatory floor), and ISCR of 1.51 leaves a thin interest-coverage buffer if borrowing costs prove sticky.

fundamental.thesis: CDSL is one of India's two securities depositories and the larger by account count (18.59 cr demat accounts, up 17.2% YoY, with 58 lakh new accounts opened in Q1FY27), so it earns from the long-term rise in household investing, though its income still rises and falls with market activity. Q1FY27 operating revenue was about ₹293 cr, up 13.1% YoY (the segment figures add up to this; the ₹341 cr row appears to include other income), and PAT was ₹118 cr, up about 15% YoY. That continues a recovery from -5% revenue growth in Q2FY26, +12.1% in Q3FY26 and only +3% revenue with -14% PAT for FY26 as a whole, while PAT margin has held around 40% (41.1% → 39.8% → 40.1%) and is not expanding. Because CDSL is a fee-based market-infrastructure business and not a lender, I graded valuation on P/E and EV/EBITDA, not P/B. At 62x trailing P/E, 46x forward and 42.8x EV/EBITDA it sits in the 79th–92nd percentile of the broad market, the mean sell-side target is only 7.4% above the price, and 90-day EPS estimates have been cut about 1.1%, so I grade it expensive even after allowing a premium for its duopoly position. The biggest risk is that a long risk-off phase, with weak breadth and heavy foreign selling, cuts trading volumes, new account openings and IPO activity, which would hit a revenue base priced for steady mid-teens growth.

Fortis Healthcare runs a large hospital network of about 6,300 operational beds plus a diagnostics arm of about 400 labs, and it grows through occupancy, revenue per patient and adding beds. In Q2 FY27, revenue rose 17.3% YoY to Rs 2,735 cr, with growth essentially flat over five periods (17.3% to 17.8%, with only a slight recent easing), helped by 72% hospital occupancy and about 7% growth in revenue per patient, but PAT fell 2.5% to Rs 320 cr and PAT margin dropped from 14.1% to 11.7%; lower exceptional gains (Rs 3 cr vs Rs 24 cr) explain only about 1 point of that drop, and even excluding them PAT grew only about 4% by my pre-tax-unadjusted estimate. Using EV/EBITDA as the yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock is expensive at 35.6x vs a sector median of 23.3x (P81), and a trailing P/E of 69.3x vs a forward P/E of 40.9x implies about 69% EPS growth, although the mostly pharma peer set makes the comparison imperfect and the 34% consensus upside looks overstated because the 52-week position implies a price near Rs 957, or about 15% upside to the Rs 1,098 mean target. The biggest risk is that revenue growth keeps failing to reach profit while FY EPS estimates, already cut 5.8% over 90 days, fall further against a valuation that needs a sharp earnings rebound.

fundamental.thesis: IFCI is a government-owned Development Financial Institution effectively in run-off mode — its active lending business has collapsed, with the loan book shrinking -23.56% YoY to ₹1,194cr, and the company now derives income primarily from residual assets and investments rather than fresh origination. FY26 revenue grew a modest +2.5% to ₹2,069cr and PAT rose +5.7% to ₹181cr, with PAT margin recovering from -2.1% (H1FY25) to 8.7% (FY26), a directional positive — but this improvement reflects the tail of provisioning cycles on a dying book, not a genuine lending franchise revival; Gross NPA stands at a catastrophic 95.79% and CAR is deeply negative at -18.78%, far below RBI's regulatory minimum, meaning IFCI is technically insolvent on a banking capital-adequacy basis. Using P/B + ROE (the correct yardstick for a lender per the Sector Card — NOT P/E), P/B of 2.43× against an implied ROE of roughly 2% (₹181cr PAT ÷ ~₹9,100cr implied book) signals expensive — the P/B > 1.5 with ROE < 12% heuristic squarely flags this; trailing P/E of 119.29× (vs 12–18× bank sector median) confirms the same; forward P/E of 23.38× implies a heroic earnings recovery that is entirely dependent on the DFS-approved group consolidation/restructuring, a binary outcome with no earnings visibility. The single biggest risk is that the pending merger/amalgamation of IFCI subsidiaries fails to deliver value to minority shareholders, while the negative CRAR (-18.78%) and near-total NPA book leave no fundamental floor — any positive thesis is a restructuring bet, not a lending franchise bet.

fundamental.thesis: NIACL is India's largest PSU general insurer (85.44% government-owned), writing motor, health, marine, and fire coverage domestically and internationally, with a regulatory solvency ratio of 1.80×; however, the franchise is structurally loss-making at the underwriting level and profits depend entirely on investment income. Q1 FY27 delivered a net loss of ₹244 cr (vs. +₹392 cr in Q1 FY26, –162% YoY) as the incurred claim ratio worsened to 102.97% and the combined ratio deteriorated to 121.14%, confirming that claims and expenses together exceed earned premiums — both motor (–₹126 cr underwriting loss) and health (–₹134 cr) dragged, and net earned premium growth decelerated to just +1.9% YoY. Using P/B + ROE as the correct yardstick for an insurer (not P/E), P/B of 0.76× ranks NIACL at P1 in the broad peer set and appears cheap on its face, but a TTM ROE of only 3.4% fully explains this discount — it is structural cheapness, not mispricing — and analyst EPS estimates have been cut –47% in just 30 days, a classic pre-derating signal that the forward P/E of 9.2× bakes in recovery assumptions the combined-ratio trend does not yet support. The dominant near-term risk is a qualified audit conclusion on unreconciled reinsurance recoverable balances (₹75,490L gross, ₹13,783L doubtful-debt provision), compounded by a new CMD appointment in September 2026 and a mandatory Ind AS accounting transition due April 2027, leaving both governance and accounting transparency materially unresolved.

Using P/B against ROE, the right yardstick for a lender, valuation is fair at 2.71x book for a 13.0% ROE (about 2.5x on reported net worth of Rs 4,049 cr), with the 22.43x trailing P/E inside the 18-28x NBFC range only as a cross-check, while the P29 peer rank carries little weight because it compares against the broad market and the stated +38.8% target upside looks overstated because the 52-week position implies a price near Rs 92, or about +26%. The biggest risk is that fast loan growth is outrunning the safety cushion: gross NPA improved from 2.77% to 2.6%, but net NPA is stuck near 1.5%, provision coverage fell from 46.2% to 42.2%, and debt-to-equity rose from 1.80 to 2.31.

fundamental.thesis: BEML is a Schedule-'A' defence PSU under India's Ministry of Defence, manufacturing heavy equipment across mining, construction, defence platforms, and metro/rail segments, with revenue heavily dependent on government order execution. Q1FY27 revenue accelerated to ₹820 cr (+29.3% YoY from ₹634 cr) and the operating loss narrowed substantially (EBITDA swung from -₹41 cr to +₹3.6 cr YoY), yet PAT remained negative at -₹27 cr (-3.3% margin); more critically, FY26 full-year PAT collapsed 49.7% and order inflows landed at only ₹1,286 cr vs a ₹6,800 cr target — an 81% miss that is the single most important leading indicator for an order-book business. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for a capital-intensive industrial (Sector Card guidance), the stock trades at 48.4× (P88 among peers, 107% premium to sector median 23.3×) and trailing P/E of 94× versus the sector benchmark range of 28–45×, placing it firmly in expensive territory despite a more palatable forward P/E of 28× that already discounts a sharp earnings recovery. The biggest risk is that FY27 order inflows remain structurally below target, eroding book-to-revenue cover and triggering a 30–50% de-rating (consistent with Industrials sector card cycle-risk warning) before the earnings recovery the valuation demands actually materialises.

fundamental.thesis: Cochin Shipyard (COCHINSHIP) is India's largest PSU shipyard executing defence (Navy/Coast Guard) and commercial vessel contracts, backed by an order book of ₹21,100 cr (~5× annualised revenue) that provides multi-year execution visibility — structurally the most compelling asset on the balance sheet. Revenue growth has decelerated from +38.5% YoY in Q1 FY26 to +15.5% for 9M FY26, but more critically, PAT has swung sharply negative (-18.5% YoY in 9M FY26 vs +7.8% in Q1 FY26) as EBITDA margins compressed from 28.0% to 21.3% — a classic fixed-price-contract cost-creep pattern, likely driven by ISRF ramp-up overheads and higher input/subcontracting costs; cash conversion is deeply negative (CFO/PAT -2.40×, FCF -₹812 cr in H1 FY26), which is the most immediate red flag. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive model per the sector card, 45.51× sits at the upper bound of the 28–45× Industrials range and at P86 in the broad market (95% premium to median), grading expensive; the forward P/E discount (33.25× vs 54× trailing) signals the street is pricing in a sharp earnings recovery — but that recovery has not yet appeared in filed numbers and Q1 FY27 extraction is blank despite the August 2026 filing date. The single biggest risk is that margin compression deepens further on the ISRF ramp and rising crude-linked operating costs, in a RISK_OFF macro with D/E at 28.47 — any slippage in earnings recovery would unwind the current rich valuation quickly.

fundamental.thesis: Emmvee is an integrated solar module and cell maker with 10.3 GW of installed module capacity, 2.94 GW of TOPCon cell capacity and an order book of 10.4 GW. EBITDA margin is flat at around 35%, and new orders in Q2 were only 1.5 GW against 10.3 GW of module capacity running at 44% utilisation. No separate quarterly breakdown was available, so these are half-year figures. On the yardstick for capital-intensive businesses, it looks cheap: EV/EBITDA is 13.4x (P21, 42% below the broad-market median of 23.3x), trailing P/E is 19.5x (below the 28–45x Industrials range) and forward P/E is 13.7x. Together these suggest margins may fall back as module supply catches up.

Revenue growth has slowed sharply, from +48.6% in Q3 FY26 to +23.0% in Q1 FY27 and about +11.6% in Q2 FY27 (about Rs 4,188 cr, derived as H1 minus Q1), while EBITDA margin has fallen from 43.8% to about 37.4%; Q2 PAT was about Rs 65 cr, up from Rs 35 cr but only a 1.6% margin, and the growth is coming from non-aero and pricing rather than traffic (Delhi non-aero +20.3%, Hyderabad aero -8.3%, H1 traffic +1%). On EV/EBITDA, the yardstick I used because P/E (850x trailing) means little at this thin profit level, the stock is fair at 25.1x, about 8% above the broad-market median (P56), but this is a broad-market comparison with no close airport peers, and upside looks limited at 98% of the 52-week range with a forward P/E of 82.6x (P98). fundamental.thesis: Bank of India is a government-controlled public sector bank (73.4% government ownership) with a ₹9.27 lakh crore deposit base, growing advances about 16% YoY in FY26 against roughly 13.6% deposit growth. Gross NPA improved from 2.26% (Q3FY26) to 1.98% (FY26), and provision coverage rose to 94.45% in H1FY27. Profit growth is therefore coming from lower credit costs and other income, not from lending spreads, and the Q2FY27 results filed on 2026-10-23 have not been extracted yet, so the latest-quarter trend is unconfirmed. On the lender yardstick (price-to-book plus ROE), the stock trades at 0.74x book against a 12-15% ROE, the cheapest in its 15-bank peer set on P/B (P0) and about 50% below the 1.5x median, which grades as cheap. The main risk is margin squeeze: loans are growing faster than deposits, NII growth is flat, and the rate-cut cycle is repricing loan yields down faster than deposit costs, which could stall earnings once the boost from lower provisioning fades.

fundamental.thesis: Biocon is a vertically integrated biopharma holding three businesses — biosimilars (~60% of consolidated revenue, 26% EBITDA margin, 16% FY26 growth), generics (~18%), and CRDMO/Syngene (~22%) — with meaningful global positions in insulin ($300M franchise), adalimumab, and oncology biosimilars (23.5% US oncology share). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive, highly-leveraged business (D/E 42×, net debt $1.1B, interest burden ₹210–220 cr/quarter), the stock trades at 23.3× — exactly at the sector peer median (P50), which I grade as fair; trailing P/E of 147.6× is distorted by exceptionally thin PAT margins, but forward P/E of 35.5× (P69 vs peers) signals the market has already priced in a significant earnings recovery that management has guided for H2FY27. The key risk is that sell-side EPS estimates have been cut 16% over the last 90 days, CRDMO growth remains stalled on a single-client biological headwind, and the entire PAT recovery narrative rests on H2FY27 biosimilar scaling and interest-cost step-down delivering simultaneously — any slippage on either leg derails the deleveraging path.

fundamental.thesis: Balkrishna Industries (BKT) is India's dominant specialty off-highway tire (OHT) manufacturer — serving agricultural, industrial, and construction segments globally with ~6% global OHT market share — with heavy export dependence on Europe and a capital-intensive manufacturing model that makes EV/EBITDA the primary valuation yardstick. EV/EBITDA of 19.5x (the appropriate primary yardstick for this capital-intensive manufacturer) sits at sector midpoint (P60 vs peers), while trailing P/E of 29.7x — slightly above the 18–28x Auto sector benchmark — looks far more attractive in peer context: BKT sits at P20 in its sector with a 24% discount to peer median of 39.2x, and forward P/E of 21.5x vs trailing 29.7x signals the market is pricing in a meaningful earnings recovery, making the stock fair-to-slightly-cheap on a relative basis. The core risk is that JLR's four planned BEV launches fail to fill the Jaguar volume gap while high leverage leaves no cushion for further margin disappointment.

On the sector card's yardstick for steel (EV/EBITDA, 5–8x at mid-cycle), 14.2x is expensive; it only looks fair against the 16-peer median (P33) because that median includes paint and adhesive companies, and the cheap forward P/E of 12.2x relies on earnings roughly tripling just as FY estimates have been cut 13.3% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that higher interest costs on expansion debt, plus the weak Mauritius subsidiary (₹3,113 cr accumulated losses, ₹4,769 cr parent loan), keep absorbing volume gains while crude, a strong dollar and the risk-off market squeeze steel spreads.
